A biology teacher studies the diastolic blood pressure of a population of $N = 450$ male students in a high school. He measured the diastolic blood pressure of a sample of $n = 50$ male students. Given that the population mean diastolic blood pressure, in millimeters of mercury ($mmHg$), is $μ = 70$ with population standard deviation $σ = 8$, what is the probability that the mean diastolic blood pressure of the male students in the sample is more than $68mmHg$?

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $z$ | $0.05$ | $0.06$ | $0.07$ | $0.08$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $-1.9$ | $0.0256$ | $0.0250$ | $0.0244$ | $0.0239$ |
| $-1.8$ | $0.0322$ | $0.0314$ | $0.0307$ | $0.0301$ |
| $-1.7$ | $0.0401$ | $0.0392$ | $0.0384$ | $0.0375$ |
